speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome to the clinic. I need to understand your dizziness and vertigo better to help you. Are you experiencing spinning sensations, or does the room feel like it's tilting when you move your head?

speaker: Patient
text: 70-year-old woman. The patient presents with sudden episodes of dizziness that are position dependent. She describes experiencing a false sensation of motion and occasional spinning, indicative of vertigo. She denies any recent illnesses, injuries, or significant changes in health status, apart from age-related hearing loss (presbycusis).

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for that detailed description; the "false sensation of motion" triggered by head movement is very specific. Given your age and position-dependent symptoms, have you noticed any new hearing loss, ringing in your ears (tinnitus), or a feeling of fullness in the affected ear during these episodes?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Episodes of dizziness and spinning sensation. I also have Position dependent vertigo, No recent illness, No hearing loss besides presbycusis.

speaker: Doctor
text: The symptoms you describe—position-dependent vertigo with no hearing loss—are classic for Benign Paroxysmal Positional Vertigo (BPPV). To confirm this, would you mind performing the Dix-Hallpike maneuver for me right now? REQUEST IMAGES: [None]

speaker: Patient
text: Past medical history: No significant past medical or surgical history. No history of Meniere's disease, vestibular neuritis, or labyrinthitis. Social history: Retired school teacher. Lives alone. Non-smoker, occasional wine. Enjoys light gardening.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Benign Paroxysmal Positional Vertigo (BPPV). Your history of position-dependent vertigo, age, and absence of neurological deficits or hearing loss strongly support this diagnosis.
